# Psalm 76 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choir director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song. God has made himself known in Judah; his name is celebrated throughout Israel.

**2** He set up his tent in Jerusalem and made Zion his home.

**3** Right there he snapped the fiery arrows, shattered the shields, the swords — all the weapons of war. Selah

**4** You shine with glory, more majestic than mountains full of game.

**5** The bravest warriors were stripped of everything; they fell into the sleep of death, and even the mightiest soldiers couldn't lift a hand.

**6** At the blast of your voice, God of Jacob, both horse and chariot were frozen in their tracks.

**7** You — you are terrifying! Who could possibly stand in your presence when your anger erupts?

**8** You thundered your verdict from heaven; the earth trembled and fell silent,

**9** when God stood up to pass judgment and to rescue every oppressed person on earth. Selah

**10** Even human rage ends up bringing you praise; what's left of their fury you strap on like a belt.

**11** Make promises to the LORD your God and keep them! Let everyone around him bring gifts to the one who should be feared —

**12** the one who humbles the proud rulers and terrifies the kings of the earth.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **76:3-6**: The image is stunning: God doesn't defeat the enemy in a long battle. He just shows up and everything stops — arrows snap, warriors collapse, horses freeze. It's over before it starts.

- **76:10**: This is one of the most mind-bending verses in the Psalms. Human rage, which is meant to destroy God's purposes, somehow ends up serving them. Even evil can't escape God's sovereignty.

— PNEUMA
